summary: qwen-mt-turbo (the production translator) retires 2026-10-10. A successor must pass strict masked-name token survival, match turbo-class quality, and fit the 5-minute cron budget. The 2026-09-29 off-QwenCloud provider sweep re-measured 12 open-weight models on both directions plus the masked set. Disqualified below does NOT mean bad at translation — the DeepSeek models are the best pure translators measured — it means unusable for THIS production pipeline, which masks people's names before translation and restores them afterwards. The 2026-09-29 identity spike (docs/identity-spike.md) then showed the PUA token scheme itself breaks weak tokenizers: switching the masks to ASCII brackets [[n]] fixes glm-4.7-flash, glm-5.3-flash and nemotron outright, so masking-scheme migration + re-measurement is the next step.

why: 10/10 masked-name token survival in both directions
73.71 chrF id->en (+1.8 over the retiring qwen-mt-turbo, +2.0 over the QwenCloud interim pick)
84.66 chrF en->id (turbo-class; direction re-measured on the balanced 78-segment set)
non-thinking: no reasoning leakage, no mid-sweep stalls, 1.4-1.6 s/segment
cheapest safe model measured: a full two-direction sweep costs about two cents

alternatives.why: best token-safe id->en off QwenCloud (74.21, Kagi-level) at 5-8x the price; take it if id->en quality is worth the premium or as a second vendor for drift checks
73.39 id->en, 10/10 survival both directions, maker-diverse from the primary
72.72 id->en, 10/10 survival both directions, permissive Gemma licence

disqualified.reason: the best raw translation quality in the entire table (deepseek-flash: 77.10 chrF id->en — above Kagi and every other model — and 87.05 en->id) AND YET unusable here: production masks names into placeholder tokens before translating, and DeepSeek drops them in the production direction (id->en survival 9/10, 6/10, 7/10 — e.g. 'Ben and Wiwit suggest registering before the 15th' came back as '5 and 3 suggest that participants register…'). chrF cannot see names; the Token survival toggle can. Caveat from the identity spike: deepseek-v4-flash passed all six masking schemes 20/20 under the same preservation clause, so the drops are not yet reproduced — re-verify with a fresh masked run before treating this as model truth (docs/identity-spike.md).

fails masked survival en->id (7/10); its endpoint also mandates reasoning. The identity spike traced the mechanism: its tokenizer cannot emit PUA placeholder characters and renders them as bare digits (8/10) — with ASCII brackets [[n]] it survives 10/10, so it is scheme-broken, not identity-broken.

mangles PUA placeholder tokens into bare digits or invented <n> tags (14/20) and drops curly-brace markers occasionally (19/20) — must not be the outage failover on the current PUA scheme. With ASCII markers ([[n]], NME{n}X, <name-n>) it survives 20/20, so the failure is the scheme, not the model (docs/identity-spike.md).
fail id->en masked survival (2/10, 1/10); qwen-mt-lite passes raw but inherits the family's non-raisable caps and single-vendor retirement risk

caveats: token-safe models run 1.4-2.7 s/segment sequential: a 300-segment entry needs 3-4 concurrent requests to hold the 5-minute cron budget; QwenCloud's qwen-flash (0.46 s/s, 10/10 survival, raisable limits) remains the sub-minute option if staying on QwenCloud
the survival assertion + review flags stay regardless of model: the turbo baseline production trusted also failed the adversarial probe set
qwen-mt-turbo retires 2026-10-10; until the switch, it remains the production model
